purpose: Section 23: predeclared root-cause hypothesis evidence ratings for the STEP_MATCHED_INTERLEAVED_MULTI_FAMILY predictor's known-family conformal calibration failure.

H1_INSUFFICIENT_CALIBRATION_SUPPORT.evidence_for: Development-holdout n per (family, depth) is small (16), so per-depth coverage estimates carry wide Wilson 90% CIs (e.g. loop-grid depth 12 seed 20260814: [0.545, 0.882]).
H1_INSUFFICIENT_CALIBRATION_SUPPORT.evidence_against: Calibration n per (family, depth_bucket) is 100-150 (m9-3-support-analysis.json), giving a finite-sample resolution of ~1% -- not small in absolute terms. Quantile-bootstrap resampling (m9-3-quantile-stability.json) shows loop-grid's MATURE quantile is STABLE (relative span 0.04-0.11 across seeds), not noisy. The counterfactual decomposition (m9-3-counterfactual-diagnostics.json) shows that even the MOST pooled/highest-support variant (D, BROAD_FALLBACK_CONTROL) gives essentially the SAME loop-grid MATURE coverage (0.75) as the tightest family:depth grouping (A) -- more calibration support at the SAME distributional composition would not close this gap.
H1_INSUFFICIENT_CALIBRATION_SUPPORT.cross_seed_consistency: ROBUST (quantile stability and counterfactual-equivalence findings hold on all 3 seeds)
H1_INSUFFICIENT_CALIBRATION_SUPPORT.limitations: Small per-depth development n does add genuine descriptive uncertainty to any single depth-level coverage estimate; family-pooled (n=112) estimates are much tighter and are what this milestone leans on for the primary claim.

H2_CALIBRATION_DEVELOPMENT_SHIFT.evidence_for: For loop-grid MATURE, the required_quantile_shift (development-oracle quantile minus the actual CURRENT_FAMILY_DEPTH quantile) is robustly positive across all 3 seeds: +0.040, +0.051, +0.057 (m9-3-counterfactual-diagnostics.json). Development p90 nonconformity score exceeds calibration p90 by ~0.05-0.06 at loop-grid MATURE on every seed (m9-3-score-shift.json), i.e. development's upper tail is harder than calibration's upper tail even though medians nearly match.
H2_CALIBRATION_DEVELOPMENT_SHIFT.evidence_against: KS test between calibration and development score distributions at loop-grid MATURE is not classically significant (p~0.18-0.20 on all 3 seeds), and median scores are nearly identical (~0.80 both splits) -- this is a TAIL-CONCENTRATED shift, not a bulk distributional shift, and a naive whole-distribution test under-detects it.
H2_CALIBRATION_DEVELOPMENT_SHIFT.mechanism_established: See H7 below: the shift has a concrete, mechanistic explanation in scenario-generation source-node coverage, not merely a bare statistical observation.
H2_CALIBRATION_DEVELOPMENT_SHIFT.cross_seed_consistency: ROBUST (required_quantile_shift positive and of similar magnitude, 0.04-0.057, on all 3 seeds)
H2_CALIBRATION_DEVELOPMENT_SHIFT.limitations: Development n=112/family limits statistical power of the KS test itself; the shift is established primarily through the counterfactual-oracle comparison and tail statistics, not through KS significance.

H3_INTERLEAVED_OVERCONFIDENCE.evidence_for: None found on the one family (golden-reference) where ARM_A and ARM_B2 can be directly compared on identical incidents.
H3_INTERLEAVED_OVERCONFIDENCE.evidence_against: At depth 1 (golden-reference), ARM_B2's mean max-probability is LOWER than ARM_A's both when correct (0.657 vs 0.818) and incorrect (0.543 vs 0.714) -- ARM_B2 is less confident, not more. At depth 6, ARM_B2's incorrect predictions have HIGHER entropy (0.217 vs 0.110) and LOWER mean max-probability (0.912 vs 0.944) than ARM_A's incorrect predictions -- again less peaked/overconfident, not more (m9-3-confidence-analysis.json). At MATURE depths (12, 25) both arms are 100% correct on golden-reference (n=16, no incorrect examples for either), so no failure-mode confidence comparison is possible there.
H3_INTERLEAVED_OVERCONFIDENCE.cross_seed_consistency: Checked on seed 20260814 in depth; qualitatively consistent direction expected on other seeds given the effect size, not exhaustively re-verified per seed in this writeup -- see m9-3-confidence-analysis.json for full per-seed detail.
H3_INTERLEAVED_OVERCONFIDENCE.limitations: This comparison is only possible on golden-reference (ARM_A's only known family), so H3 cannot be directly tested for branched-loop/loop-grid where the actual coverage failure is concentrated. The negative finding is scoped to golden-reference only.

H4_FAMILY_SCORE_HETEROGENEITY.evidence_for: MATURE-bucket calibration quantiles differ dramatically by family under the identical ARM_B2 predictor: golden-reference 0.18-0.64 (seed-dependent, near-zero nonconformity -- very easy) vs branched-loop 0.92-0.94 and loop-grid 0.92-0.93 (consistently high nonconformity -- hard), on every seed (m9-3-support-analysis.json). Family-pooled marginal development coverage is correspondingly stratified: golden-reference 0.946-0.955 (robustly above the 0.85 floor), branched-loop 0.79-0.875 (borderline), loop-grid 0.71-0.73 (robustly below the floor), identical ordering on all 3 seeds.
H4_FAMILY_SCORE_HETEROGENEITY.evidence_against: None -- this is the most unambiguous finding in the study.
H4_FAMILY_SCORE_HETEROGENEITY.cross_seed_consistency: ROBUST -- identical family ordering and comparable magnitudes on all 3 seeds.
H4_FAMILY_SCORE_HETEROGENEITY.limitations: ARM_A (single-family baseline) has no second known family to compute cross-family heterogeneity against, so this milestone cannot cleanly separate "heterogeneity is intrinsic to comparing diverse topologies" from "heterogeneity is specifically induced by interleaved training" -- only that it is present and severe once multiple diverse families are evaluated under one predictor.

H5_DEPTH_CONDITIONAL_FAILURE.evidence_for: Depth-of-failure is family-SPECIFIC and clearly patterned, not MATURE-concentrated as a universal rule: golden-reference's only meaningful undercoverage is at depth 6 (MID, 0.812 on all 3 seeds) and depth 1 (0.875); its MATURE coverage (12, 25) is a perfect 1.0 on every seed. branched-loop's undercoverage concentrates at EARLY depths 1-3 (0.625-0.875); its MID/MATURE coverage is close to or above the floor on 2 of 3 seeds. loop-grid is undercovered UNIFORMLY across essentially every depth (0.625-0.75 at depths 1 through 25 alike) -- not concentrated at any single depth (m9-3-depth-analysis.json).
H5_DEPTH_CONDITIONAL_FAILURE.evidence_against: loop-grid itself does NOT show a depth-concentrated pattern -- its failure is uniform across depth, so H5 does not explain loop-grid's own failure (the dominant contributor to the pooled known-family undercoverage).
H5_DEPTH_CONDITIONAL_FAILURE.cross_seed_consistency: ROBUST per-family depth pattern (golden-reference always worst at depth 6; branched-loop always worst at EARLY; loop-grid uniformly bad) on all 3 seeds.
H5_DEPTH_CONDITIONAL_FAILURE.limitations: This is a real, robust, family-conditional pattern, but it is secondary to H4/H6/H7 for explaining the DOMINANT contributor (loop-grid) to the overall known-family coverage failure.

H6_SPECIFIC_FAMILY_FAILURE.evidence_for: loop-grid family-pooled coverage (n=112/seed) is 0.712-0.732 with Wilson 90% CIs [0.64-0.65, 0.79-0.80] on all 3 seeds -- CI ENTIRELY below the 0.85 floor, no overlap, on every seed. golden-reference is CI-entirely-above-floor on every seed (0.90-0.98). branched-loop is the mixed/intermediate case (2 of 3 seeds close to or above floor, 1 seed, 20260815, clearly below at 0.7946). Refined further: WITHIN loop-grid, a single source node (J1) has coverage exactly 0.214 (6/28) on ALL THREE seeds (identical, since development scenarios are shared across seeds by M9.0a's own design) while J2-J4 range 0.82-1.0 -- one node single-handedly drags the family average down. The same pattern (one much-weaker node, JC at 0.679) appears within branched-loop.
H6_SPECIFIC_FAMILY_FAILURE.evidence_against: None for loop-grid; branched-loop is a genuinely intermediate/mixed case, not a clean pass.
H6_SPECIFIC_FAMILY_FAILURE.cross_seed_consistency: ROBUST at both the family level and the source-node level (J1's 0.214 coverage is bit-for-bit identical across all 3 seeds).
H6_SPECIFIC_FAMILY_FAILURE.limitations: The extreme cross-seed identicalness of J1's coverage (exactly 6/28 every seed) reflects that development scenarios are a SHARED, non-resampled pool across seeds (by design, per M9.0a's protocol) -- this is expected, not independent confirmation from 3 statistically distinct samples; it does mean the finding is a property of that specific set of development scenarios.

H7_IMPLEMENTATION_OR_DATA_DEFECT.M9_3_STATUS: NOT_AN_ENGINEERING_BLOCKER -- a documented, mechanistically-explained dataset/eval-design finding, not a bug in M9.3's own diagnostic code (the Section-5 reproduction gate passed EXACTLY, confirming M9.3's table-construction code is faithful to M9.0a/M9.0b) or a defect in the conformal code path itself (m9-3-implementation-audit.json found no defect there).
H7_IMPLEMENTATION_OR_DATA_DEFECT.evidence_for: The exchangeability audit (m9-3-exchangeability-audit.json) found that development-holdout source-node coverage for loop-grid is EXACTLY {J1, J2, J3, J4} at 25% each -- J5 through J8 (4 of loop-grid's 8 junctions) never appear in the development population at all. branched-loop similarly only exercises {JA, JB, JC, JD} of its 7 junctions. golden-reference has exactly 4 junctions, so it is the ONLY family where development exercises the FULL source-node space -- and it is also the ONLY family with robustly-passing coverage. This traces to a concrete, deterministic mechanism in the shared, FROZEN M7/M9.0/M9.0a evaluation harness: `run_m7_topology._generate_eval_scenarios`'s `EVAL_MAX_SOURCES=4` constant combined with `sources = junctions[:min(EVAL_MAX_SOURCES, len(junctions))]` (alphabetically sorted, then truncated) -- while the CALIBRATION pool (`_family_scenario_pool`) draws source_node via the scenario generator's own broader/randomized process across the FULL junction set. This is a genuine calibration-vs-development population mismatch for any TRAINED family with more than 4 junctions, present identically on every seed because it is a deterministic property of already-frozen code, not data variance.
H7_IMPLEMENTATION_OR_DATA_DEFECT.evidence_against: This mechanism alone does not fully explain WHY J1 specifically (as opposed to J2/J3/J4, which ARE in the tested subset) is so much harder (0.214 vs 0.82-1.0) -- the truncation explains WHICH nodes are tested, not why one of the tested nodes is intrinsically harder. The J1-specific difficulty (persistently confused with J7/J8 at every depth, per m9-3-miscoverage-cases.json case D/E) may be a genuine structural/hydraulic source-discrimination property of the loop-grid topology, not purely an artifact of the truncation.
H7_IMPLEMENTATION_OR_DATA_DEFECT.cross_seed_consistency: ROBUST -- this is a deterministic code property, identical on every seed by construction.
H7_IMPLEMENTATION_OR_DATA_DEFECT.limitations: This finding is about the FROZEN, already-existing M7/M9.0/M9.0a/M9.0b evaluation harness, which M9.3 reused unmodified (per governance) and did not alter. M9.3 did not verify the calibration pool's OWN source-node distribution is genuinely uniform/full-coverage (only that it uses a different, less-truncated construction) -- this would need direct instrumentation of `_family_scenario_pool`'s random source assignment, not attempted here to avoid modifying frozen code.

H8_CURRENT_SCORE_INCOMPATIBILITY.evidence_against: The identical nonconformity score (1 - p_true), quantile formula, and calibrator machinery achieve robustly-passing coverage (0.90-0.98) for golden-reference under the SAME predictor and SAME alpha=0.1 -- the score itself is clearly capable of supporting nominal/floor coverage when the calibration and development populations are representative of each other. The failure is localized to specific families/source-nodes with a documented representativeness problem (H7), not a general property of this score choice under this predictor.
H8_CURRENT_SCORE_INCOMPATIBILITY.cross_seed_consistency: ROBUST (golden-reference passes on all 3 seeds under the identical score).

overall_synthesis: The known-family calibration failure is NOT a single, uniform phenomenon. It decomposes into: (1) a ROBUST, STRONGLY-SUPPORTED family-and-source-node-level heterogeneity (H4, H6) that is (2) mechanistically explained by a concrete, deterministic dataset/eval-generator defect (H7) in the shared, frozen M7 evaluation harness -- development-holdout scenarios for any trained family with more than 4 junctions systematically exclude a majority of that family's source nodes, while calibration draws from the full set. This produces a real calibration-vs-development distribution mismatch concentrated in the score distribution's upper tail (H2), NOT explained by insufficient calibration support (H1 weak), interleaved-predictor overconfidence (H3 not supported), or a defective nonconformity score (H8 not supported). A secondary, family-conditional depth pattern exists (H5) but does not explain the dominant loop-grid failure, which is uniform across depth.
